# General EDA, with a focus on basic graphing 

```{r}
# Libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
# Read in data
clean <- read.csv("clean.csv")
head(clean)
```

```{r}
# Graphing unemployment rate over time
ggplot(clean, aes(x = date, y = value)) +
  geom_line(color = "#BCD2EE", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "#BCD2EE", size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Unemployment Rate Over Time (Monthly)",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Unemployment %",
    subtitle = "U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Local Area Unemployment Statistics"
  ) +
  theme_dark(base_size = 14)

```

```{r}
# Positive/Negative Graph on Unemployment Net Change
clean %>%
  mutate(
    change = as.numeric(x1_month_net_change),
    month = as.integer(str_remove(period, "M")),
    date = as.Date(paste(year, month, "01", sep = "-"))
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(date, change)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#BCD2EE") +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Month-to-Month Net Change", x = "Date", y = "% Change",
    subtitle = "U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Local Area Unemployment Statistics") +
  theme_dark()
```


```{r}
# Density of unemployment percentages
clean %>%
  mutate(value = as.numeric(value)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_density(fill = "#BCD2EE", alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(
    x = "Unemployment %",
    y = "Density",
    title = "Density of Unemployment %",
    subtitle = "U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Local Area Unemployment Statistics"
  )+
  theme_dark()
```

```{r}
# Unemployment over time per state

mix %>%
  mutate(
    value = as.numeric(value),
    month = as.integer(str_remove(period, "M")),
    date = as.Date(paste(year, month, "01", sep = "-"))
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(date, value)) +
  geom_line(color = '#BCD2EE', linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ state, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_dark() +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Over Time by State",
    subtitle = "U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Local Area Unemployment Statistics", y = "Unemployment", x = "Year")
```
